datasheet.title: EX2300-C Compact Ethernet Switch datasheet, document 1000580-017-JP (Juniper Networks, September 2021)

description: Juniper EX2300-C-12P is the compact, fanless member of the EX2300 line: a 1RU-high Gigabit Ethernet access switch 279 mm wide with 12 10/100/1000BASE-T ports, all with PoE+ and 124 W available, and two built-in 10-Gigabit SFP+/SFP uplink ports. The front carries the 12 jacks in two stacked rows numbered 0 to 11 (the upper jack of a column takes the even number), the two uplinks numbered 0 and 1, a USB port, the management Ethernet port with the RJ-45 console port under it, a mini-USB console port, three status lamps, four port-mode lamps, a Factory Reset/Mode button and an ESD point. The rear carries the earthing terminal, a heatsink and the AC power cord inlet; there are no fans. The power supply is built into the chassis, so there are no bays. It ships standing on its rubber feet; it can also be fixed under a desk, to a wall or a ferrous surface, or on two posts of a rack with the separately orderable brackets. The -TAA and -VC part numbers are the same chassis. The EX2300-C-12T is the same front without PoE.

name: ex2300-c-12p

airflow.note: The cooling system "consists of the vents on the top of the chassis and the heatsinks installed in the rear panel in PoE models"; there are no fans, so the chassis is passive.

built-in-power-and-fans.note: Hardware guide, Power Supply in EX2300 Switches: "The power supply in EX2300 switches is built in along the rear panel of the chassis"; Table 2 lists "Switch with built-in power supply" and, for the fan, "EX2300-C switches are fanless models". Nothing in the guide describes removing or replacing the supply. It is part of the chassis, not a bay and not a component, and there are no fans.

chassis.note: Table 3: height 1.72 in (4.36 cm), width 10.98 in (27.9 cm), 18.86 in (47.9 cm) with the mounting brackets attached, depth 9.45 in (23.8 cm), weight 6.99 lb (3.17 kg). 279.0 x 43.6 x 238.0 is carried, the metric as printed. The datasheet (Table 1 and physical specifications) gives 27.9 x 4.4 x 23.9 cm (10.98 x 1.72 x 9.4 in) and 1 RU; the guide's depth is used, 1 mm shallower, because it is the guide's own metric and inch figures that disagree (9.45 in is 240 mm) and the printed metric is the one the other EX2300 devices carry. The photographs show the end caps (the ribbed bumpers) inside the 279 mm and no ears.

colour.note: median of the bare front plate in the photograph (#676d71).

esd-point.note: photo-measured - Figure 1 callout 10: the ESD point is a banana jack on the left of the face with the ESD triangle beside it, drawn as a stroked triangle mark (the library's ESD sticker is wider than the printed symbol and would cover the jack). A second, smaller hole under it in the photograph carries no printing and is not named by the guide, so it is not drawn.

front-console.note: estimated - the mini-USB console port (guide Figure 1, callout 7) is drawn as chassis art, a 7.9 x 4.6 mm shell with its opening, the size the other EX2300 devices carry and the 12P photograph agrees with (about 8 mm across, 4.5 mm high). It is not a component: the library has no mini-USB receptacle and its DCIM export has no row for one.

front-layout.note: estimated - read off the front photograph as described under gate-1. The 12 jacks stand in one shell of six columns, the first jack at 38.4 mm, 13.97 apart, the rows 14.1 mm apart (cell tops, tab included) with the upper row turned 180 so its keyway and lamps are above, as the photograph shows. The two SFP+ cages stand 33.9 mm apart (the cage centres at 148.0 and 181.9 mm), each with a LINK lamp over an ST lamp on its left. The USB-A port is upright (turned 90). The management and console jacks are one stacked housing, 17.4 mm wide, with the management jack on top turned 180 (its two green windows are above it, as the photograph shows); the console jack is the lower one. The mini-USB console port is drawn as chassis art. The two ribbed end caps are read off the same photograph. The photograph shows two small corner marks (a sticker frame) beside the uplinks and above the USB port that the guide's Figure 1 does not draw; neither carries printing and neither is drawn.

gate-1.note: The front photograph is 1500 x 300 px with the body (bumper to bumper) 1462 px across: 5.240 px per mm against the 279 mm of Table 3. The ganged jack pitch then reads 73.4 px = 14.0 mm, the 13.97 the registry records for the ganged RJ-45 cell, on a quantity the scale never saw. The photograph is 6.11 across to down (bumpers included) against the table's 279 / 43.6 = 6.40, so y is taken at the same 5.240 px per mm with the body centred on the bumper extent (the face top at 35.5 px); the guide's Figure 1 (1500 x 463 px, body 1244 px across) shows the same aspect, 6.07, so it does not pass the aspect check either and is used for what is on the face and for confirming order, not for absolute y. Every position is therefore estimated and good to about a millimetre.

heatsink.note: photo-measured - Figure 7 callout 4: PoE models carry a finned heatsink along the rear (a black ribbed block, 165 mm across), and the guide says EX2300-C switches have no exhaust openings, so it is drawn as a vent field because that is how it reads, not as an opening: nothing is cut in the rear.

lamps.note: Hardware guide, Tables 4 to 12 and Figures 16, 20, 24, 25 and 27. Each RJ-45 port and uplink has two lamps, Link/Activity and Status; the RJ-45 lamps are in the jack housings (Figure 24), the uplink lamps are the LINK and ST pairs the photograph prints beside each cage (Figure 25). The Status lamp reads out whichever of SPD, DX, EN and PoE the Factory Reset/Mode button has selected, shown by which port-mode lamp is lit. SYS is green, ALM red or yellow and MST green. The management jack's two windows are Link/Activity and Status (Tables 6 and 7). The jack lamps keep the component's link and activity vocabulary because a block cannot override it per lamp.

mounting.note: Table 35 and Table 34: the switch ships standing on four preinstalled rubber feet; it mounts on or under a desk or level surface, on a wall by screws, on or under a ferrous surface with the separately orderable magnet-mount kit, and on two posts of a 19 in rack or cabinet (also a four-post one) with mounting brackets and screws that are "separately orderable for EX2300-C switches"; it cannot be mounted recessed. The guide gives no part number for the EX2300-C bracket kit, the wall screws, the magnet-mount kit, the cable guard kit or the cable lock kit, so none is listed and no ear position is stated; the datasheet states a height of 1 RU, so the chassis is a rack device of 1 RU and a viewer that asks for ears gets the generic pair. The cable guard and the security slot (on the right panel) are accessories and chassis furniture the guide does not draw flat.

port-numbering.note: photo-measured - the photograph prints each column's two numbers in orange under the shell, the even number up and left and the odd number down and right (0 and 1, 2 and 3, ... 10 and 11), so the upper jack takes the even number; the two uplinks print 0 and 1 in white under their cages. Port numbers are as printed on the metal, from 0. The Junos interface names are not printed: the guide's Table 2 gives PIC 0 as 12x10/100/1000 Base-T and PIC 1 as 2x10G SFP/SFP+, i.e. ge-0/0/0 to ge-0/0/11 and xe-0/1/0 and xe-0/1/1; they are recorded here and not in an interfaces block because the faceplate does not print them.

power.note: Table 14: maximum power consumed by the switch 24 W when no PoE power is drawn, maximum PoE/PoE+ power available 124 W; Table 15: 100 through 240 VAC, 50/60 Hz, 2.5 A at 100 VAC and 1.25 A at 240 VAC. The rear legend of Figure 7 and the datasheet's power rating (170 W AC) are recorded and not carried.

rear-layout.note: estimated - positions off the rear photograph (1500 x 300 px, 5.20 px per mm across, the face top at 31.6 px): the two earthing holes with the earth symbol, the heatsink, the four screws beside it and the AC inlet, which agree with Figure 7. The serial number label in the photograph is a paper label carrying a real serial number, so no label is drawn, and the guide's drawn serial number and CLEI rectangles (callouts 1 and 2) are left out for the same reason. The photograph prints the legend over the inlet; the guide's Figure 7 prints it vertically beside the inlet, as drawn here.
